subject.title: Prompt-cache prefix churn on OpenAI models: per-turn dynamic injections (message tool hint + volatile system-prompt section) defeat automatic prefix caching

question: Should OpenClaw move `message_tool_only` visible-reply guidance out of tool descriptions and cache-sensitive system prompt content for OpenAI/Codex paths?
rationale: The source-backed churn is real, but the permanent fix changes the owner boundary between delivery enforcement, prompt steering, and provider cache behavior.

options.title: Approve stable-prefix repair
options.body: Move the per-turn delivery directive into late turn content while keeping message delivery enforcement in runtime code and requiring live OpenAI cache proof.

options.title: Require telemetry first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers collect current-main `gpt-5.5` cache traces that quantify the remaining loss after recent partial fixes.

options.title: Preserve current delivery prompt
options.body: Accept the cache cost for now to avoid risking visible-reply regressions in `message_tool_only` channels.

recommendation.title: Approve stable-prefix repair
recommendation.body: Move the per-turn delivery directive into late turn content while keeping message delivery enforcement in runtime code and requiring live OpenAI cache proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent stable binding and per-turn delivery-mode work is closest to the remaining owner boundary.
